brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,1#cut (addDrawer at cell (0,1,0), key s), offered on the cut face of the half-n base at (0,1,0).

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner of the same cell
requirements.evidence: Both are on cell (0,1,0): the spike sits at the junction of (0,0),(0,1),(1,0), which is a corner of (0,1), and the drawer is on that cell's south cut face, the side facing (0,0) and (1,0). The configurator offered both at these positions and check_build reports meshClash clear. I did not verify the exact corner point geometrically beyond that, so treat 'exact same corner' as supported by placement, not measured.
The drawer is seated on the cut face of the half base at (0,1), which the spike's junction cells share; the configurator accepted both with no mesh clash.

finish.summary: Built: half-n base at (0,1,0), full base at (0,0,0), half-w base at (1,0,0), a drawer on (0,1)'s cut face and a spike at the junction of (0,0),(0,1),(1,0). check_build: meshClash clear, no rule errors. Open items: a LOOSE_BODY warning between the half-n and half-w bases (joint bolts would lock them) and open cap faces, which are informational. I did not add these since the brief did not ask for them.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
